item.title: Why The Bali 5.4 Should be Your Next Charter
item.description: The Bali 5.4 brings together space, comfort, and performance all in an impeccably designed 54-foot catamaran perfect for charter vacations. This yacht was built with a focus on open bright living spaces, comfortable accommodations, and plentiful outdoor spaces. With room for up to 12 in its six-cabin configuration, the Bali 5.4 is perfect for social sailing. Dream Yacht guests have the option to enjoy this yacht through a cabin cruise or when the yacht has availability outside of cabin charters, book it as a crewed yacht charter for an exclusive experience with family and friends. A Layout Designed for Living The center of the Bali 5.4’s design was built around bringing people together while still allowing space to spread out. Fluid flowing spaces from bow to stern creates seamless connection between the outdoor living areas, saloon, and aft cockpit. One of the most distinctive and innovative features of this yacht is the large pivoting rear door. It excellently connects the salon with the aft cockpit creating one extended living area and allowing for a larger conversation space. Another unique feature is the sliding windows that allow for more airflow and light giving an open air feel throughout. Forward of the saloon a door provides easy access to the foredeck. Here cushioned seats stretch out into the sun allowing guests to relax and enjoy the views while underway. While the aft cockpit provides a perfect gathering space for lunch or dinner at anchor with comfortable seating. The davits and swim ladder on the stern provide an easy access to the water for swimming. Then above there is a flybridge with a large U shaped seating area perfect for sipping a morning coffee with the sunrise or sundowners after a rewarding day of cruising. Forward of the seating area find the sunbathing pads where guests can lounge while taking in the breathtaking scenery of one of Dream Yacht’s incredible destinations. This Bali 5.4 provides so many areas where connection to the natural world and each other become possible. Find peace and shared experiences through innovation and exploration aboard this yacht. Take the Tour Comfortable Accommodations Below Deck The Bali 5.4 continues to deliver through its focus on comfort as we move below deck. Each cabin is equipped with queen sized beds, a private bathroom with a shower, and adequate storage space. Natural light and airflow are still features even down in the cabins; some cabins even have direct access to the deck. For large groups this layout is meant to give everyone their own private space at night, while relishing the communal spaces during the day. Guests get the feeling of home and settling in through these comfortable areas instead of the fleeting feeling of a hotel room. Why Charter the Bali 5.4 Space for Everyone – Roughly 130 square meters of living space allows for plenty of room to dine, relax, and enjoy cruising without feeling crowded. Indoor/Outdoor Living – The yacht’s flow from bow to stern and one of a kind opening door from the saloon to the aft cabin makes it easy to roam between the interior and exterior living spaces. Enjoy the breeze blowing through the yacht which creates a light airy open feel that connects you to the natural beauty of the surrounding world. Relaxation Area Options – There is no shortage of lounging areas onboard from the flybridge to the foredeck choose your ideal spot to enjoy the sail from. Now Newly Available for Private Crewed Charters When a Bali 5.4 is not being used on a cabin charter it will be available for a private crewed charter experience with a captain and hostess. This means families or groups of friends can experience the entire yacht privately, with a professional crew taking care of the sailing, itinerary, food, and day to day operation. Allowing guests to concentrate on relaxation and taking in the scenery from any of the comfortable lounging areas. item.title: BVI Vacation Without Sailing Experience: Best Yacht Charter Options for Beginners
item.description: Picture waking up to the sound of waves against the hull of a catamaran anchored in a secluded cove in the British Virgin Islands (BVI). Walk on deck and soak up the sunshine and the spectacular views this area is famous for. It’s the perfect holiday, and the best part is that no sailing experience is needed. With Dream Yacht Worldwide , you can enjoy a BVI yacht vacation without having to know a jib from a mainsail. We make sailing accessible to all, with three options especially suited for beginners: Easy Crew, Skippered, and Cabin Cruises. Can You Go on a BVI Vacation Without Sailing Experience? Many people assume that exploring the ocean requires a formal captain’s license or a deep understanding of marine navigation. While renting a boat entirely on your own, known as a bareboat charter , requires sailing experience, there are plenty of ways to enjoy the sea without any technical knowledge. With a crewed BVI sailing vacation , you don’t need to stress about managing a vessel. Our team oversees managing the necessary tasks, such as tracking the weather, anchoring in a busy bay, or interpreting complex nautical terms. You’ll have experienced staff managing onboard systems for you while you enjoy the experience. Our modern catamarans are also stable boats, which means a very low risk of motion sickness and a comfortable stay for those new to life on the water. Best BVI Charter Options If You Don’t Know How to Sail Every traveler has a different preference when it comes to privacy, budget, and daily schedules. Dream Yacht Worldwide provides three distinct entry points designed to match your personal style. Best For Privacy Level Meals Budget Skippered Charter Families and friend groups High (Full private yacht) Cook your own meals or dine ashore Mid to High Easy Crewed Charter Milestone trips and relaxation seekers High (Full private yacht) Half or full board cooked by a host Premium Cabin Cruise Couples, solo travelers, and budget travelers Private cabin, shared deck Set meal plan included in the price Affordable BVI Skippered Yacht Charters: Ultimate Freedom and Privacy A skippered charter means you rent an entire yacht for your group and hire a professional captain to sail it. You have total control over your daily schedule, allowing you to choose exactly when to sail and which bays to visit. The captain handles all the physical labor, anchoring, and navigation, while you and your guests enjoy the exclusive use of the boat. A BVI catamaran charter with skipper is ideal for families who want to cook their own meals or try local beachside restaurants every night. BVI Crewed Yacht Charters: The Effortless Private Getaway If you want the ultimate luxury of a private boat combined with the service of an all-inclusive resort, consider an Easy Crewed charter . Along with a professional captain, you get a dedicated onboard host/cook to manage the galley and handle tasks like grocery shopping (provisioning) or cooking meals during your stay. Cabin Cruises: The Budget-Friendly Entry Point to Sailing A Cabin Cruise is a smart choice for those who want to experience the yachting lifestyle without renting an entire boat. You can book an individual, private cabin with its own bathroom on a large, modern catamaran. The journey follows a pre-planned route, and meals are prepared and served by the crew. Think of it as staying at a boutique hotel that drops anchor at a different, beautiful spot every day. Why the BVI Is Ideal for First-Time Yacht Vacations The British Virgin Islands are widely considered the sailing capital of the Caribbean. The unique geography of the region creates a gentle, welcoming environment for anyone new to the water. Line-of-Sight Navigation and Calm Waters One of the biggest comfort factors in the BVI is that you can almost always see the next island on the horizon. item.title: Chartering A Power Catamaran With Dream Yacht Charter
item.description: Back in May we announced the exciting addition of power catamarans to our fleet, starting with initial availability in the British Virgin Islands , La Paz , and the Bahamas . But what do these FP Maestro 37ft yachts offer in terms of pros? We’ve put together the key benefits of how power catamarans offer a whole new experience for our charterers. Top power catamaran benefits Speed: It goes without saying that motor yachts tend to be a lot faster than sail yachts. Motor yachts like the FP Maestro 37 can hit up to 22 knots or so, depending on the sea conditions, which gives a great sense of freedom for thrill seekers. Sail yachts hit around 9-10 knots and are completely reliant on sea and wind conditions, plus the skills of the crew Efficiency: The extra 10 knots you have on a motor yacht means you can make the most of your vacation time. You can cover distances in half the time it takes a sail yacht, making motor yachts the perfect choice for island hopping and going short distances. This is why we featured motor yachts at our most popular island hopping and line of sight sailing destinations, so you can have more time exploring favourite islands or discovering new locations Clearance: Motor yachts also have low clearance, which means they are ideal for going under low bridges Relaxation: Their lack of a mast also makes motor yachts a perfect grab n’ go charter boat, as you won’t have to worry about raising or lowering sails. This means you won’t have to call your guests to be all hands on deck, but can focus on relaxing and letting the motor do the work Accessible: You can charter motor catamarans with just power boat experience on your bareboat resume. This means they are a great way for someone who may want to charter in international waters but have yet to gain sailing experience. If you don’t have any sailing or power boat experience, we can also book a professional captain to handle the vessel for you Our team is here to answer any questions to share current charter pricing and availability of our new lineup of FP Maestro 37s, just call our office at 855-650-8902 or email us . item.title: Sailing Croatia: 5 UNESCO World Heritage Sites You Can Visit By Yacht
item.description: Between sparkling sapphire beaches, enchanting historic architecture, and tantalizing coastal cuisine, it’s no wonder Croatia is a trending destination for global travelers. With 1244 islands along the Adriatic coastline and an extensive network of lakes and rivers, there’s an abundance of Croatia sailing holidays to choose from. Even better, Croatia is home to 10 UNESCO World Heritage sites! These protected landmarks are carefully selected by the United Nations for their cultural significance and ‘belong to all peoples of the world.’ Excited to experience a slice of Adriatic history but prefer to stick to sailing? You’re in luck! Five of the World Heritage Sites in Croatia are located on the coast and can be easily visited during your sailing holiday . Keep reading to learn more. 5 UNESCO World Heritage Sites To See On Your Croatia Sailing Holiday UNESCO Sites Croatia: Dubrovnik Old Town Known as ‘The Pearl of the Adriatic,’ the Old Town of Dubrovnik is a time capsule to the 13th-century Mediterranean. Complete with Gothic churches, Renaissance-era palaces, and Baroque fountains, this well-preserved destination is a must for history aficionados. Of course, anyone who loves coastal charm will fall in love with Dubrovnik Old Town, too. Situated on aqua-blue water with sandy beaches and lush vegetation, Dubrovnik blends small-town magic with waterfront luxury. The best way to get a taste of Dubrovnik is to walk along the Old Town Walls, which connect the ancient fortresses encircling the UNESCO site. You’ll get a perfect view of the coastline, nearby islands, and iconic terracotta roofs sweeping across the city. As you explore the museums, churches, fountains, and palaces, be sure to include a tour (or two) of Old Town’s wine bars! As Playwright George Bernard Shaw put it, “Those who seek paradise on Earth should come to Dubrovnik.” UNESCO Sites Croatia: Plitvice Lakes National Park The otherworldly mystique of Plitvice Lakes National Park has long enchanted visitors to Croatia. With rolling hills, crystalline lakes, and cascading waterfalls, the dense forest is so magical it feels straight out of a fantasy film. Although the park’s 16 different lakes are exquisite on their own, the site’s most iconic features are the rushing waterfalls. In fact, thanks to the hilly landscape, these cascades connect each lake in a never-ending flow of sparkling mineral-rich waters. One way to experience the grottoes is on foot – 18 km of wooden pathways enable visitors to meander around the sequences of tumbling water. However, Plitvice Lakes National Park is best experienced by boat. UNESCO Sites Croatia: Historic City of Trogir Ancient history is on full display in the Historic City of Trogir . People have lived in this coastal town since the 3rd century BC, making it a remarkable example of what historians call urban continuity. But don’t let the antiquity fool you – no matter your taste, there’s plenty to do in Trogir! Fine restaurants, bars, cocktail lounges, and cafes line the cobblestone streets, tempting visitors to indulge at all hours of the day. Shopping is also a main attraction here, particularly for artisan goods and local produce, oils, and meats. Can’t get through a holiday without plenty of sweets? Trogir is also home to an entire square dedicated to ice cream. Of course, Trogir’s main attraction is boating, so it is one of the most popular destinations for a Croatia sailing holiday. From nearby islands to local watering holes, this UNESCO gem is best experienced on the water. UNESCO Sites Croatia: Stari Grad Plain on Hvar Island Sailing Croatia is incredible no matter where you go, but Stari Grad Plain on Hvar Island might be the most unique destination on your itinerary. This strip of coastal land has been preserved since the 4th century BC, when the Ionian Greeks cultivated it for agriculture and irrigation.
